concepts.name: Voltage, current and resistance
concepts.summary: Define voltage as energy per charge, current as charge flow rate and resistance as opposition to current, with their units.

concepts.name: Closed circuit loop
concepts.summary: Explain why current flows only in a complete conducting loop containing a source and how open and short circuits differ.

concepts.name: Ohm's law
concepts.summary: Relate voltage, current and resistance with V=IR and rearrange it to find any one of the three.

concepts.name: Circuit symbols and schematics
concepts.summary: Recognise standard symbols for sources, resistors, capacitors, inductors, switches and ground and read a simple schematic.

concepts.name: Series and parallel connections
concepts.summary: Distinguish series (same current) from parallel (same voltage) arrangements and say what each does to current and voltage.

concepts.name: Electrical power
concepts.summary: Explain power as the rate of energy transfer and compute it with P=VI, I²R or V²/R.

misconceptions.text: Current is used up as it flows through a resistor, so less current leaves than enters.
A battery supplies a fixed current regardless of what is connected to it.
Ohm's law means every component has constant resistance whatever the voltage across it.

concepts.name: Equivalent resistance
concepts.summary: Reduce series and parallel resistor combinations step by step to a single equivalent resistance.

concepts.name: Voltage and current dividers
concepts.summary: Apply divider formulas to find the voltage across or current through a branch without solving the full circuit.

concepts.name: Capacitor and inductor behaviour
concepts.summary: Describe a capacitor storing energy in an electric field (i=C dv/dt) and an inductor in a magnetic field (v=L di/dt).

concepts.name: Ideal sources and loading
concepts.summary: Distinguish ideal voltage and current sources and explain how internal resistance makes a real source's output drop under load.

concepts.name: Passive sign convention
concepts.summary: Assign reference polarities and current directions consistently so that signs of power and voltage are interpreted correctly.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's current law
concepts.summary: Apply conservation of charge at a node so that currents entering equal currents leaving.

concepts.name: Kirchhoff's voltage law
concepts.summary: Apply the fact that voltages around any closed loop sum to zero, with consistent sign conventions.

misconceptions.text: Parallel resistors add up like series resistors, so adding a parallel branch raises total resistance.
Current in a series circuit is shared out between components, so a component later in the chain gets less current.
An ideal voltage source always delivers the same current no matter the load.

concepts.name: Node-voltage analysis
concepts.summary: Choose a reference node, write KCL equations in terms of node voltages and solve the resulting linear system.

concepts.name: Mesh-current analysis
concepts.summary: Assign mesh currents in a planar circuit, write KVL equations and solve for branch currents.

concepts.name: Superposition principle
concepts.summary: Find a response by summing contributions of each independent source acting alone, with others deactivated, in linear circuits.

concepts.name: Thevenin and Norton equivalents
concepts.summary: Replace a linear network seen from two terminals by a source with a series or parallel resistance and convert between the two forms.

concepts.name: Maximum power transfer
concepts.summary: Show that a load receives maximum power from a source when its resistance equals the Thevenin resistance and analyse the efficiency cost.

concepts.name: First-order RC and RL transients
aliases: step response of RC and RL
concepts.summary: Derive and use exponential charging and discharging responses with time constants τ=RC and τ=L/R from initial and final conditions.

concepts.name: Dependent sources
concepts.summary: Include voltage- or current-controlled sources in nodal, mesh and equivalent-circuit analysis.

misconceptions.text: Superposition can be used to add up the powers dissipated due to each source separately.
To deactivate sources in superposition or Thevenin, replace every source with an open circuit.
Maximum power transfer means the circuit is operating at maximum efficiency.

concepts.name: Phasor representation
concepts.summary: Represent steady-state sinusoids as complex numbers carrying amplitude and phase and convert between time and phasor domains.

concepts.name: Impedance and admittance
concepts.summary: Model R, L and C as complex impedances and combine them with series and parallel rules.

concepts.name: Phasor-domain circuit analysis
concepts.summary: Apply KVL, KCL, nodal, mesh, Thevenin and superposition to AC circuits using complex arithmetic.

concepts.name: AC power and power factor
concepts.summary: Evaluate real, reactive and apparent power, and judge power-factor correction for a given load.

concepts.name: Resonance in RLC circuits
concepts.summary: Analyse resonant frequency, Q factor and bandwidth of series and parallel RLC circuits.

concepts.name: Frequency response and filters
concepts.summary: Assess the magnitude and phase response of RC and RL networks and choose low-pass, high-pass or band-pass behaviour for a purpose.

concepts.name: Second-order transient response
concepts.summary: Classify RLC step responses as overdamped, critically damped or underdamped from the characteristic equation.

misconceptions.text: Phasor analysis describes the whole response, including the switch-on transient.
Voltages across series elements in AC simply add as magnitudes, like in DC.
Reactive power is wasted energy dissipated as heat in the load.

concepts.name: Laplace transform of circuits with initial conditions
concepts.summary: Judge when to transform a circuit to the s-domain, using initial-condition sources, to obtain complete transient and steady-state responses and transfer functions.

concepts.name: Pole-zero stability analysis
concepts.summary: Judge circuit behaviour, damping and stability from pole and zero locations of a transfer function.

concepts.name: Two-port network modelling
concepts.summary: Construct and interconnect two-port parameter models to characterise subcircuits by terminal behaviour.

concepts.name: Three-phase power systems
concepts.summary: Evaluate balanced wye and delta three-phase circuits using per-phase analysis and line versus phase quantities.

concepts.name: Coupled inductors and transformers
concepts.summary: Analyse mutually coupled circuits and judge transformer models for impedance matching and isolation.

concepts.name: Non-ideal component and parasitic effects
concepts.summary: Evaluate how resistance, parasitic capacitance and inductance, and ESR alter ideal circuit predictions at various frequencies.

concepts.name: Circuit design under constraints
concepts.summary: Design a network to meet specifications while accounting for tolerances and for source and load impedance, using pole-zero and two-port models.

misconceptions.text: Ideal lumped-element models remain accurate at any frequency and component size.
Per-phase analysis works for any three-phase circuit, even unbalanced ones, without modification.
Any circuit with all poles in the left half-plane is automatically well-behaved, with no need to check damping or sensitivity.
